span.label: behavioral priming, OPERATIONALLY - and the inclusion criteria are the definition: word primes, INCIDENTALLY presented, a NON-OPPOSITE control group, and a BEHAVIOURAL dependent variable. Each clause excludes something. `Incidentally` rules out instruction; `behavioral dependent variable` rules out the judgement studies that most of this corpus's priming records use; and `non-opposite control` quietly excludes designs whose control condition primes the contrary concept, which would double the apparent effect
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the effect, as a NUMBER rather than as an existence claim: d(FE) = 0.332, d(RE) = 0.352 across 352 effect sizes from 133 studies. `Small` is the paper's own word for it. The corpus holds dozens of records asserting that priming happens; this is the one that says HOW MUCH, and the size is what most of the surrounding controversy is actually about
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: goal activation versus perception-behavior, ADJUDICATED WITHOUT A WINNER BEING DECLARED. The finding is an INCREMENT - goal activation `contributes over and above` perception-behavior - not a replacement. Two mechanisms this corpus has been collecting from separate papers, measured against each other for the first time, and the answer is both
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A MODERATOR NULL REPORTED IN THE ABSTRACT - expectancy, the perceived probability of achieving the goal, did not moderate priming. It was predicted to matter by two literatures that disagree about the DIRECTION (Forster: high expectancy strengthens pursuit; Locke & Latham: difficult goals intensify effort), so a null defeats both. A meta-analysis that puts its non-finding in the abstract alongside its finding
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the ideomotor inheritance, with the awkward part named: the perception-behavior account follows James's ideomotor model `ALBEIT WITHOUT THE CONSCIOUS (IDEO) COMPONENT FROM JAMES`. A mechanism borrowed from a nineteenth-century theory of voluntary action, with the consciousness that gave it its name removed - stated in the review's own parenthesis rather than dug out by a critic
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → prior priming meta-analyses (Cameron, Brown-Iannuzzi, & Payne, 2012; DeCoster & Claypool, 2004; Van den Bussche, Van den Noortgate, & Reynvoet, 2009)

span.label: goal activation —contrasted-with→ perception-behavior
span.note: differs in: WHAT THE PRIME INSTALLS - a goal that pursues an outcome, against a direct perception-to-action potentiation. The meta-analysis finds the goal account adds explanatory work OVER AND ABOVE the perceptual one rather than replacing it, which is why this is contrasted-with and not distinct-from · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE ADJUDICATION. Two mechanisms the corpus has been collecting from separate papers - Bargh2001 for goals, the ideomotor tradition for perception-behavior - weighed against each other over 352 effect sizes. The answer is an increment, not a winner, and the weight says so.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: expectancy —causes→ priming effects
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.9 — A NULL RECORDED AS A DIRECTION, which is what `no-change` exists for. Two opposed literatures each predicted expectancy would matter - Forster (high expectancy strengthens pursuit) and Locke & Latham (difficult goals intensify effort) - and neither is supported. It is in the abstract, where a null is easiest to leave out.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: behavioral priming —same-as→ priming effects
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — The two names are used for one thing inside a single argument - `if BEHAVIORAL PRIMING requires goal-mediated processes, no PRIMING EFFECTS should emerge`. Weighted 0.85 rather than higher because the paper never states the identity; it displays it. Recording it is what lets a reader see why the paper's findings and its theory are phrased differently.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
